citations.review_text: Great story, let down by some occasionally buggy gameplay (seemed to be related to playing without VSync enabled)

Great narrative game, engaging enough stealth and combat. NOTE: on modern hardware, there are a couple difficulties - if anything feels weirdly hard, crank the resolution scaling to 200% - a lot of the physics is framerate-based so you must lower it by doing this. You can play 95% of the game normally, but if you need certain tripod things to turn to the right, or need all the rats to not go at the same time, tank the frame rate.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention experiencing a specific progression-blocking tent bug in Chapter 6 that requires changing display settings to escape.

citations.review_text: Awesome game nothing crazy hard there is one bug i see a lot of people having too. I think its on chapter 5 or 6 with the tent you get stuck if you are full screen. what you have to do is switch it to boarder less screen  and then it will let you get out but other then that zero bugs great game

The game looks pretty good for a game that came out in 2019. The devs created their own engine to create the rat swarms and I don't think there is any other game with this kind of rendering of swarms of rats. The game feels scenic with charming voice acting and immersive scenery. 

However, this feels like more of an interactive story than a game. The gameplay mechanics are extremely one dimensional and simple. And to top that off it becomes repetetive. The "puzzles" are just for name. This is also mirrored by extremely dumb AI and linear level design. The ammo types are too diverse and switching between them is clunky.

The light mechanic feels awry similar to Alan Wake. While the story is told in a decent manner, there is hardly a moment that connects with you. The NPC charactrers are again one-dimensional and lack any depth at all. There are many stealth and supposed to be intese moments which never really make you tense.

Finally, the controls on PC feel very floaty. Almost 50% of the times Amicia can't run because you are talking or walking etc. The last few levels felt extremely laborious.

There is a tent bug in Chapter 6 for which you need to look up a Youtube video. Game optimization also does not scale for max (uiltra) settings for all options. I saw framedrops in outdoors playing at 165 fps while it runs smoothly indoors with massive rat swarms.

I will give it maybe 5 or 6/10 and do not reccommend.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features a linear level design with simple puzzles and straightforward stealth mechanics.

citations.review_text:
It's a fine game in general if you consider it a pure walking simulator with some extra elements. But considering this a real game is what leads me to give it a thumbs down. The story is full of plot holes and unrealistic elements. For example, there's an abandoned place that apparently hasn't been visited in a very, very long time, yet somehow there's a torch that's still lit (?)

There are some weird conversations that sometimes don't make much sense and feel forced. The gameplay is okay for a walking simulator (and it's honestly the only thing that kept me playing until the end). The combat starts off simple and then adds more things to do later in the game. The puzzles, however, are insultingly easy. I used my fingers to solve them more than my brain. 

Edited: I don't know, maybe it's just not my taste. The first chapters are very, very promising. It even has a Dark Souls-style boss fight, but I feel like those things are just there to hook you. The real game has less and less as you keep playing. The more you play, the less you can see what makes this game good. GG, but it's a thumbs down from me.

Very linear game, with easy puzzles and easy stealth. But it has some really good storytelling, with good voice acting and characters. Every level looks amazing from a visual point of view, and it contributes strongly to the game's vibe, making it very immersive. The whole gameplay system is designed around the rats' crowd AI, and it's very cool. I love it when a game tries new things. I really thought it was going to be a boring game, but new gameplay elements kept getting added, and the cinematic gameplay parts were very engaging.

It's a short game, but definitely worth buying at a good discount.

A Plague Tale: Innocence is a great story-driven game set in 14th-century France, where you control a girl named Amicia trying to save her little brother Hugo from both ruthless guards and thousands of flesh-eating rats. The game has an emotional story, a amazing dark atmosphere, and fun puzzles using light and fire to avoid the rats, though it is quite linear and the enemy AI can be a bit too easy. The storyline is a 9/10 and the game has no bugs or flaws, yet I wouldn't play it again because it's not particularly ultra great.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat and controls as clunky or unresponsive, particularly when aiming or handling items and moving large objects.

citations.review_text:
Things I thought were good (keeping in mind that this is a 2019 game reviewed in 2026):
- Atmosphere is fantastic, if a bit overdone in points. This feels like an actual world that the characters exist in, levels are sufficiently creepy and dark.
- I like the idea of kids as the playable characters, it brings something new to the table, and when they ACT like kids it really helps with immersion.
- Having multiple characters in my party, with different personalities, is a strong bonus.
- Graphics are well done, as is environmental sounds. Voice acting is great.

Things I didn't like
- This is definitely a dumbed-down game built for controllers, not KBM. Everything feels poorly responsive, especially when moving items, like pushing a cart
- FULL of invisible walls. You'll be running down a path and hit the end of the zone with nothing visible stopping you. You can't get closer than a couple of feet away from a river unless the story tells you to.
- Dumb enemies - you can be carrying a torch inches from a guards back, and they won't notice you. If the story tells a guard to follow a path, or watch a specific brick on the wall, that's what they will do forever without variation.
- Instant lethality. If a guard ever DOES notice you, you'll be reloading from last checkpoint.
- Hand holding - everything you can pick up is glowing silver and you'll spot it from across the map. Anytime you need to climb, the ledge is painted white. If you need to break something with your sling, it's always a glowing target and often also prompts you to hit a button to look directly at it.
- Have to do exactly what the game wants you to do, and it broadcasts that. You could be walking down a path, see a pair of guards talking, and conveniently spot a hiding spot with ammo for your sling before the guards split up. Then you'll see a crate full of glowing metal crates for you to throw a rock at, so the remaining guard will walk 6 feet and spend 20 seconds looking at the crate of shiny metal.
-…

What the frick did I just play.


TL;DR - Overall, not a good game in my opinion. Gameplay is meh, story is bad and nonsensical, ending felt unfinished, and I was glad to finish it so I could never play it again.

Gameplay-wise, the sling is neat in concept, and I like the crafting system. Puzzles were kinda fun, though everything regarding the rats was forgettable, the consumable items got too many too fast, and wowzers the aim snapping on moving targets is bad, especially since camera sensitivity is hilariously low. As for stealth, it was either boring or frustrating (except for one part later on, but then it introduced a new mechanic which ruined the game for me again). Follower AI is stupid as always... Oh, and let's not forget the few times I got softlocked!

When it comes to the story, I think the writers confused "emotional" with "kill off a bunch of characters before players can get attached to them for cheap sadness"; I felt nothing for these characters throughout the entire game. The story was also all over the place. The final hour in particular just felt... strange. I honestly hated it. It's like it was an afterthought, not a satisfying ending at all. The dialogue is also mostly stupid and forced, but very rarely there is an interaction that reminds you of actual people, and those moments are good. There is also a very short walking-cutscene right before the final part of the game that was really well done. Otherwise, the story was not compelling and pretty bad.

On top of all that, there is the fact that E for skip cutscenes cannot be rebound (I'm an ESDF player), and after you watch credits, you play another chapter and watch another set of credits. That's a first for me lol. At least you can skip them.

So yeah, with all that in mind, I have no clue what I just played and it feels like it was a poor way to spend 9 hours over the last few days.

I'm a bit conflicted about whether to give this game a thumbs up or not. The gameplay is very repetitive, the controls feel clunky and are sometimes unresponsive, and there were plenty of moments where the combat became more frustrating than enjoyable.

Nevertheless, the game has a rare and interesting medieval setting, the story is fairly decent, and the world feels alive. Characters are constantly talking, and there's almost always something happening around you, which does a lot to enhance immersion.

At full price, I can't recommend it. However, I bought it as part of a bundle with the second game, and I may come back and update this review if Requiem turns out to be significantly better.

On a deep discount, though, I'd say it's worth considering.

*EDIT: After I beat the second game, which is worse IMO. I'm giving this one thumbs up, it deserves your attention, Requiem doesn't.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has no difficulty settings.

citations.review_text:
[h1] Game about rats [/h1]

A fairly easy game overall, as long as you are patient because there is no difficulty settings.

[h2] Story & Characters [/h2]
The story has a really weak start, but the middle of the game gets much better and the ending is excellent. The main characters receive a lot of growth throughout the game and you can really see how much they have changed by the end. Although I kinda dislike how it goes because revenge becomes the main part of the narrative. It makes sense within the context of the story, but it isn't exactly an original way.

But I do wish the side characters received more development. Some of them feel like they could have been explored much further.

[h2] Stealth & Combat [/h2]
The stealth is straightforward and the levels are mostly have the same feel. The game gradually evolves from being primarily a stealth experience into more of a kill everyone approach. You get more interesting ways to plan your route but by the end your mostly encouraged to use 2-3 abilities to reach the end as killing has no consequences.

[h2] Looting & Crafting [/h2]
Looting is straightforward and encourages you to explore the levels for materials, especially if you want to upgrade your equipment or how you play the game. You will constantly find things like alcohol, sulfur, fabric, leather and other ingredients that can be used for ammunition, alchemical tools and upgrades. But it feels useless once you upgrade the sling for killing while other QOL or stealth upgrades feel not worth it anymore.

[h2] Levels & Exploration [/h2]
Most levels are fairly straightforward and usually have you moving almost in a straight line toward your destination. There are occasional alternative routes where you can find hidden items, crafting materials, or additional lore. The game does that boring job of showing you what can be climbed by using white paint on the environment.

[h2] Bugs & Issues [/h2]
The game is generally fine technically, but there are some annoying …

Went in completely blind on the story and what the gameplay truly was like. I knew it was stealth-focused...but honestly, there was plenty of janky combat. Once you get to chapters 15-16 the performance tanks and the difficulty just skyrockets. Lack of proper aim locking, NPCs not doing their actions to move the game forward. Was so excited for the finale until we got to the Rodric-pushing-cart sequence outside the cathedral gates and you need to use your sling on the 8 incoming enemies. Thankfully, I came back the next day and by a stroke of luck got past it after literally having the game make me cry in frustration. The final boss fight is intense, but somehow, after many attempts at that too, we finally were able to enjoy seeing the end of the game on stream.

I am now reluctantly going to try the second game...very worried about the random difficulty spikes and performance issues...but we shall try.

(P.S. if your game stutters a bit, make sure you are playing in borderless, not fullscreen! I have a 5080 and multi-stream and once I switched to that it helped fix).

Watch my gameplay here: https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLGF5Og6FAo3Y&si=OpuWsMmBEHnDoWPb

claims.claim: The game features simple stealth and puzzle mechanics rather than deep action or complex gameplay systems.

citations.review_text:
I didn’t expect much going into this game, but it surprised me in a good way. The atmosphere and story do most of the heavy lifting here, and that’s where the game shines. Medieval France is portrayed as a dark, filthy, and constantly dying world, yet it still manages to look beautiful in its own bleak way. Between the plague, endless rats, ruined towns, and crumbling castles, there’s always a feeling that something awful is waiting around the corner, even when nothing is happening.

The story is easily the best part. Amicia and Hugo’s relationship holds everything together, and it’s handled really well. Watching them slowly change and learn to rely on each other as things get worse was one of the main reasons I kept playing. The game gets emotional at times, and a few scenes genuinely stuck with me after I finished. That said, not everything lands perfectly. Some dialogue feels a little unnatural, and there are moments where the story expects you to accept things without giving much explanation.

Gameplay is pretty simple overall. You have stealth, some light combat with the sling, crafting, puzzles, and a lot of sneaking through dangerous areas filled with guards or rats. It all works, but none of it is especially deep. The puzzles are probably the weakest part since most of them are obvious and don’t take much effort to solve. Combat can also feel clunky, especially when things get hectic and you’re trying to aim quickly. The enemy AI has its share of dumb moments too, which can kill the tension when a guard suddenly forgets how to function.

Exploration is another area where I wish there was a bit more freedom. There are collectibles and hidden paths, but some sections don’t let you go back once you move forward. That can be frustrating if you’re trying to find everything. The controls can also feel slightly awkward during more intense moments, which doesn’t help.

Even with all that, I still really enjoyed it. The gameplay isn’t amazing on its own, but the atmo…

Really beautiful game! An emotional story with very loveable characters. The world isn't huge, but there's plenty of collectibles and materials to be found while exploring, as well as some extra achievements, and it's all so well designed. The gameplay is relatively simple and straightforward, mostly focused on stealth and the occasional puzzle. And rats. So many rats.

This is a great third-person linear adventure game with a big focus on its setting and narrative.
It takes place in a version of 14th-century France during the Black Plague and the French Inquisition. You play as Amicia and her little brother, Hugo, as they try to survive against Inquisition knights and hordes of rats.
The story is dark, mature, and interesting from beginning to end. The main duo also meets various companions during their journey, and they’re interesting as well.
Gameplay is more focused on stealth than combat, although most stealth sections feel more like puzzles, since it usually feels like there’s a proper, intended way to approach them. The main weapon, a sling, is mostly used as a tool to solve these sections. Direct combat is also discouraged, since you die in one hit. There are also more traditional puzzles.
The mechanics are on the simpler side, but they feel appropriate. There’s also some progression through a basic crafting system that requires you to gather materials during your travels. Other than that, there are some collectibles and miscellaneous achievements.
The game has good graphics and runs well. The sound design is also spot on, with good voice acting. The overall presentation is great—you can tell it was made with passion.
You can tell it’s a more budget-oriented AA title, but I was impressed. It’s a great game overall that I can easily recommend.

Game overview by A Plague Tale Wiki page:

"A Plague Tale: Innocence is an action-adventure stealth video game developed by Asobo Studio and published by Focus Entertainment. Set in Aquitaine during the early years of the Hundred Years' War, the story follows Amicia de Rune and her younger brother Hugo as they flee from the Inquisition and swarms of rats carrying the Black Death. The gameplay centers on stealth, puzzle-solving, and the use of limited tools to evade both human and supernatural threats."

My rating 7/10 

This game is both beautifully dark and bittersweet. I love that the writers didn’t shy away from a grim storyline, especially since so many modern games tend to play it safe nowadays. Hopefully, Requiem delivers that same raw tone.

I do have some pros and cons to share:

~The gameplay lacks challenge, for me at least
~The jump prompt (the spacebar in my case) was a bit buggy
~NPC AI was also buggy (RIP Lucas you died too many times thanks to this)
~Too short for my taste (though understandable from a storytelling perspective)

Pros:

~Storytelling
~Voice acting 
~THE POWER OF FRIENDSHIP 
~The sling, that thing is so fun. I should get one myself!
~An easy 100% completion for all the trophy hunters out there
~Very short, making it perfect for quick gaming sessions
~The game features replayable chapters, so if you missed an achievement you can easily get it


P.S. Do be warned if you have musophobia (or "suriphobia" if you know, you know) there are a lot of cute little rats running about in this game."

8.5/10 - a rare stealth puzzle-adventure story rich game that continues to wow 7 years after release.  Reminds me of a blend of The Last of Us and Hellblade Senua's Sacrifice.  Haunting and fitting soundtrack (particularly "Father" and "Beyond the Horizon"), emotional story, impressive cinematic visuals, unique setting (France 1348 Black Death), interesting game mechanic (rat physics and models), and memorable characters (the growth and forging of the bond between Amicia and her little brother Hugo).  

It is important to know beforehand that the navigation is linear, stealth/combat on the simpler side, some chapters move slowly, and AI is a bit befuddling at times (I moved a light away from you and you didn't notice etc).  These could be potential turn offs for those expecting more or something realistic.

For achievement hunters, this is one of the easier completions (3/10 difficulty and 15-20 hours completion).  There are collectibles and various missables to be mindful of.  Fully equipping the sling/equipment will require you to be thorough in exploring the level for materials and only crafting ammunition when you absolutely need.
